title: inspection-findings
description: The envelope one inspection of one scope writes. It is a file the agent wrote rather than anything parsed out of what it printed: a format enforced by nothing breaks silently, and a malformed finding read out of prose would be indistinguishable from no finding at all. ITS ITEMS ARE TYPED AS OBJECTS AND NOTHING MORE, and that is deliberate rather than lax. This validator subset has no reference keyword, so restating the brief's fields here would be a second definition of a shape this repository defines once in schemas/story-brief.schema.json — two definitions that agree today and drift the first time either is edited. Each finding is instead held to the brief schema on its own, which is also what makes one malformed finding cost only itself: it is dropped and named with the field that failed, and the findings beside it in the same file are filed exactly as they would have been.

findings.description: The findings this inspection of this scope produced, each of which is separately held to schemas/story-brief.schema.json. An empty array is an answer rather than an absence: it says the Inspector looked at this scope and found nothing worth filing.

area_suggestions.description: What the Inspector could name no area for, and what it thinks each such brief concerns. Optional: an envelope carrying only `findings` is what every inspection wrote before this existed and is what an inspection of a target declaring no area vocabulary goes on writing. THE SHAPE IT EXPECTS IS A LIST OF ENTRIES, each an object carrying a `slug` string — the slug of the finding this suggestion is about, spelled exactly as that finding spells it, which is how a report matches a suggestion to a brief that was actually filed — and a `concerns` string, what that brief seems to concern in the Inspector's own words, so a person can decide whether the target's vocabulary is missing a line. THE ENVELOPE HOLDS THE FIELD TO NONE OF THAT, and that is deliberate rather than lax: the pair is judged by the reader rather than by the envelope, because IT IS READ FOR THE REPORT AND FILED BY NOTHING — a suggestion never reaches a brief, a payload, an outbox entry or a tracker, since the vocabulary grows by a person editing the target's own document and a name no developer has approved must not be filed under — so a field reaching nothing may not become the thing that stops an inspection. An entry that is not a usable pair, and a field that is not a list at all, therefore yield nothing of their own and cost the entries beside them nothing, exactly as the findings loop drops one malformed finding and files the findings beside it. `orchestration/inspection.py`'s `_area_suggestions` is the filter that judges each entry. What the field buys is that a missing area is reported rather than silent, which is the whole reason naming none is a first-class answer.
